rationale: This is essentially the archive's AbnormalFinancingWeakEarnings re-plumbed with a balance-sheet net-external-financing numerator (itself the published Bradshaw–Richardson–Sloan anomaly) and IND_RANK swapped for IND_ZSCORE — a measurement/coverage variant rather than a substantively different mechanism.

The stated design ("both legs are firms with historically large buybacks") does not hold because TS_RANK of prstkc/at is degenerate under ties for the many firms with zero repurchases in all five years, so those firms still receive full-weight margin-trend exposure and the signal collapses toward a plain gross-profitability-trend sort.

The gate/payload construction is internally consistent and dividend-cut conditioning is genuinely unused in this archive, though the cutter population is small enough that both extreme deciles will be heavily diluted with zero-signal non-cutters, blunting the long-short spread.

Using gross repayment rather than net issuance is a legitimate new instrument and the sign logic is coherent, but the product of large dltr/at with low cash ROA is close to a leverage-times-distress composite, so it risks rediscovering the financial-distress return pattern rather than a new refinancing-pressure effect.

This is the net-external-financing anomaly (Bradshaw–Richardson–Sloan) with an internal-funds deflator substituted for assets — a scaling change to a known, heavily mined signal, and the MAX(MA(oancf,3), dp) denominator can be near-zero for asset-light firms, making the extreme legs winsorization artifacts.

The change-in-net-issuance payload is a policy reversal rather than a level, which is genuinely distinct from the mined issuance-level anomaly, and the accrual gate is signed consistently with the negative expectation; the main weakness is that "accruals > 0" is a coarse near-median split that conditions weakly on earnings quality.
